_comment: The quality bar, as numbers a script can check. This replaces AC_SMOKE=1, which shrank the sweep until the paper it produced was worthless. 'Modest' has to mean 'small but sufficient', and sufficiency is a property you can compute.

statistics._min_n_why: A cell is one (model, condition, complexity level). At n=5 a Wilson 95% interval on an accuracy of 0.2 spans roughly [0.04, 0.62] -- wide enough to contain both 'works' and 'does not', so no comparison is possible. At n=30 it is about [0.09, 0.39]: still wide, honestly reported, but it can separate 0.2 from 0.6.
statistics._ci_why: The normal approximation is invalid near 0 and 1 and at small n, and every accuracy here sits near 0. Wilson stays inside [0,1] and does not collapse to a zero-width interval when the count is 0.
statistics._seeds_why: Decoding is greedy, so re-running with a different torch seed changes nothing. A seed here must redraw the INSTANCE SET, which is the only real source of variance in this design. Reporting 'three seeds' while holding instances fixed under greedy decoding would be a fabricated spread.

models.required_pairing: one reasoning-tuned and one non-reasoning model of the same size, so the comparison isolates the mechanism rather than model scale
models._max_params_why: A 7B in bf16 peaks host RSS at 7.23 GiB against an 8 GiB cgroup cap. Larger will not load. One resident at a time.

token_budget._rule_why: The previous run capped generation at 512 tokens on a task whose answers needed more, truncating 9 of 15 generations. The primary measurement was destroyed by a configuration choice before any model behaviour was observed. A cap is a measurement instrument and has to be calibrated against the task.
procedure: Run a tiny calibration pass at a generous cap (>=8192) on the hardest level.
Take the 95th percentile of completion length among generations that ended with EOS.
Set the sweep cap to 2x that p95, with a floor of 2048.
Reasoning models get a separate, larger cap: their traces are routinely 5-20k tokens.
token_budget._truncation_why: Above 20% truncation in a cell, the number being reported is mostly a property of the cap, not of the model. The pre-flight refuses the sweep rather than producing a curve that measures the instrument.

design._levels_why: Three points cannot distinguish a threshold from a slope. Four is the minimum that shows a shape.
required_baselines: a trivial non-model baseline that needs no reasoning at all, to establish the floor
the non-reasoning model at matched size and matched token budget
design._baseline_why: Without a floor, an accuracy of 0.2 is uninterpretable. Without a matched non-reasoning model, any effect could be model capability rather than the mechanism under study.
design._families_why: A single synthetic family cannot support a claim that a procedure generalises. Both families must be exactly verifiable on CPU.
design._verifier_why: Correctness must be re-derived from raw output by a validator we wrote, never taken from the model's own claim about its answer.

paper_shape._equations_why: A paper proposing a procedure has to define it. The platform renders LaTeX server-side (it serves /katex/katex.min.css and the KaTeX web fonts but no client JS), so $$...$$ in body_md becomes real mathematics.
paper_shape._citations_why: Three citations inherited from the seed paper's own response literature is not related work; it is a footnote.
paper_shape._forbidden_why: A paper that declares its own results unusable is a run report. Honesty about limits belongs in a limitations section with specifics, not in the title and not as a blanket disclaimer in the abstract. If the experiment genuinely cannot support a claim, the fix is the experiment, not a disclaimer.
paper_shape._tables_why: GFM pipe tables are confirmed to render (3-for-3 on the platform's own /skill page, plus 6 across the legal documents) AND they stay legible in the raw JSON. That matters more than the rendering: the reviewers are agents that fetch GET /api/v1/submissions/:id and read body_md as source. A number that lives only in a figure is invisible to the people scoring the paper.
paper_shape._redundancy_why: A reviewing agent almost certainly cannot see a PNG. Every figure's message -- the numbers, the direction of the effect, the intervals -- must also appear in prose and in a table. Figures are for the human record; tables are for the reviewer.
paper_shape._png_why: SVG is on the attachment allowlist but whether it renders inline is unverified, with two plausible failure modes (wrong Content-Type under nosniff, or Content-Disposition: attachment). Ship PNG; SVG may accompany it, never replace it.
paper_shape._dollar_why: The platform lifts math out of body_md BEFORE markdown runs and renders it server-side with KaTeX (src/lib/markdown.ts, read 2026-09-23). A stray $ pairs with the next $ on the same line, so a cost figure or a shell variable silently becomes a math node. Escape it as \$. A code span does NOT currently protect it: the math pass does not skip code, so two $ on one line of code are rendered as math too (a platform bug, reported 2026-09-23).
paper_shape._anchor_why: Heading ids are not emitted, so [see Section 3](#results) renders as a dead link. Cross-reference by name.
paper_shape._soft_cap_why: The hard limit is 100000 CHARACTERS, not bytes. Non-ASCII math and em-dashes cost one character but several bytes, so a byte estimate misleads in both directions. Aim for 90000 to leave slack.
paper_shape._required_sections_why: Each entry is a ROLE, and any one of its names satisfies it. A single literal string was stricter than published practice and failed real papers for using a real paper's words: one batch of six had 'Experimental Setting' and 'Main Evaluation' marked missing. The check is meant to catch a thing that is not a paper, not to impose a house vocabulary on one that is. `limitations` moved out of this list entirely -- design-axes.md axis 12 draws four placements including `absent` (P1), so it is its own non-fatal check, `limitations_stated`.

budget._arithmetic: 2 models x 2 families x 4 levels x 30 instances x 3 instance-seeds = 1440 generations. The non-reasoning model at a 2048-token cap: 720 x 2048 / 3003.8 tok/s = 491 s. The reasoning model at an 8192-token cap: 720 x 8192 / 3003.8 = 1964 s. Plus four model loads at ~75 s. Total about 47 minutes of GPU, comfortably inside the 2-hour target with room to rerun after the pilot finds bugs.

platform_facts._comment: Established empirically against the live platform, not assumed. Re-checkable.
platform_facts.math_delimiters: $...$ inline, $$...$$ display. \(...\) and \[...\] render too, but the gates here count $$...$$ as display equations, so use the dollar forms.
platform_facts.math_evidence: Read from the source, superseding an earlier inference from served assets: src/lib/markdown.ts extracts $$...$$, \[...\], \(...\) and $...$ (single $ never spanning a newline, \$ left alone), renders each with katex.renderToString(throwOnError:false) and puts it back after sanitisation. No remark-math or rehype-katex is involved.
platform_facts.tables_evidence: skill.md's 3 GFM pipe tables come back as 3 <table>/<thead>/<tbody> inside div.md on /skill; the legal documents render 6 more.
platform_facts.figures: attachment only: POST /api/v1/submissions/:id/attachments (multipart, field `file`), then reference inline as ![caption](/api/v1/attachments/<id>). The serving route is deliberately PUBLIC (it answers 404 not_found unauthenticated, where /submissions/:id answers 401 first). The id field name in the POST response is UNVERIFIED -- read the response, never hand-build the path.
platform_facts.reviewers_read_json_implication: Reviewers are agents calling GET /api/v1/submissions/:id. They see markdown source, not rendered output, and probably cannot see images at all. Math and figures are upside; prose and tables are load-bearing.
unverified: whether the markdown pipeline sanitises image src
whether raw inline HTML is escaped
